_comment: Standing government CCS funding programmes, per country. This is the register that answers 'how much public money is behind CCS in this country, over what period, and how much of it has actually gone out the door'. It exists because the news corpus cannot answer that: the corpus is a rolling window of recent reporting, so a commitment made before the window — the UK's £21.7bn, announced October 2024 — is simply invisible to it, and a country's whole funding position can appear to be a single small grant. Programmes here are the authoritative funding measure on the dashboard; the corpus supplies the separate, clearly-labelled 'new money reported this window' signal.

definitions.amount: Headline size of the pot in its own currency. NOT annual unless period_years is 1.
definitions.period_years: Years the pot is stated to run over. This is the field the corpus never had, and its absence is what made a 25-year programme look like this year's spending.
definitions.awarded_to_date: How much has actually been awarded, contracted or paid out so far, where a source states it. null means no source gives a figure — which is the common case and must not be read as zero.

scope.ccs-specific: The pot exists for CCS/CCUS. Its full value is CCS money.
scope.ccs-eligible: A broader decarbonisation pot where CCS is one eligible use among others. Its full value must NOT be read as CCS funding.

status.announced: Stated intention; not yet legislated or contracted.

programmes.awarded_note: No cumulative drawdown figure is published. Individual awards are visible as they occur — e.g. the £65.5m Viking development-fund grant in July 2026 (corpus record 2026-07-16#01) — but these are drawdown against the programme, not additional money.
programmes.quote: the UK government announced up to £21.7 billion pounds of funding support over the next 25 years for two CCS clusters
programmes.note: The single largest CCS funding commitment by any government in this register. At £21.7bn over 25 years the simple average is ~£870m a year, but the profile is not flat — early years are construction-heavy. Treat the annual average as an ordering aid, not a budget line.

programmes.quote: a £960 million fund for CCUS, greenhouse gas removals (GGRs), and hydrogen
programmes.note: Shared across CCUS, greenhouse-gas removal and hydrogen — the CCS share is not broken out.

programmes.awarded_note: Nearly US$2.2bn awarded or in award negotiations as at June 2024 — about 18% of the appropriation.
programmes.quote: Nearly US$2.2 billion of the BIL’s US$12.5 billion appropriations for carbon management have been awarded or are in negotiations
programmes.note: The clearest published example of the gap between a headline appropriation and money actually moving: roughly four-fifths of this pot was still unawarded nearly three years after the law passed.

programmes.awarded_note: Up to US$1.2bn selected for two hubs (Louisiana and Texas), each targeting 1 Mtpa.
programmes.quote: two DAC hubs, each with a total capacity of 1 Mtpa, have been selected by the Department of Energy (DOE) for significant financial support from a US$3.5 billion funding pool
$85/tonne for CO2 storage in saline geologic formations from industrial and power generation facilities
programmes.note: Uncapped per-tonne credit rather than a fixed pot, so it has no headline total: US$60/t for utilisation or EOR storage, US$85/t for saline storage, rising to US$130/t and US$180/t respectively for direct air capture. Its eventual cost depends entirely on how much CO2 is actually stored — which is why it cannot be compared against a capped programme like the UK's.

programmes.programme: Canada Growth Fund — carbon contracts for difference
programmes.quote: Up to CA$7 billion of CGF’s $15 billion in capital can be allocated to CCfDs
programmes.note: A ceiling within the CA$15bn Canada Growth Fund, not a ring-fenced CCS pot: up to CA$7bn may go to carbon contracts for difference, which cover more than CCS.

programmes.awarded_note: State funding is committed to the project and largely deployed — Northern Lights began storing CO2 in 2025.
programmes.quote: the Norwegian government provided NOK 16.8 billion of the total NOK 21.1 billion capital expenditure for project Longship
programmes.note: The state carries NOK 16.8bn of a NOK 21.1bn total — roughly 80% public. Unusually for this register, the money has actually been spent and the facility is operating.

programmes.quote: a new call for proposals under the Innovation Fund, with a record budget of €4 billion for the deployment of decarbonisation technologies, including CCS and CDR
programmes.note: A single call covering decarbonisation technologies generally, with CCS and carbon removal eligible. Earlier rounds funded Northern Lights.

programmes.quote: Sweden secured approval from the Commission under the state aid rules to allocate €3 billion to support CCS projects aimed at reducing emissions from biomass combustion or processing
the first tranche of a planned 10-year, US$130 billion climate bond ... 20% is expected to be earmarked for CCS
programmes.note: DERIVED FIGURE, not a stated one: 20% of the US$130bn ten-year climate transition bond, as the report says is expected to be earmarked for CCS. The 20% is an expectation, so treat this as indicative.

programmes.quote: the government provided AU$556.1 million over 10 years for ... Geoscience Australia to comprehensively map Australia’s subsurface resources
programmes.note: Maps subsurface resources broadly, including but not limited to CO2 storage potential. It funds knowledge, not deployment — Australia has no CCS deployment pot of comparable scale in this register.

programmes.awarded_note: Competitive support mechanisms expected from mid-2026; nothing awarded yet.
programmes.quote: Federal government earmarks €5 bn of industrial-decarbonisation support to seed first commercial CCS hubs

programmes.awarded_note: Payments begin in 2030 when capture starts; nothing has been paid yet.
programmes.quote: a 15-year, inflation-indexed contract-for-difference at €117/t (DKK 875/t) covering up to 1.25 Mtpa
programmes.note: A worked example of why period matters: DKK 16.5bn (~€2.2bn) is a 15-year obligation starting in 2030, worth roughly €147m a year, not a lump sum available today.

programmes.awarded_note: Expenditure Finance Committee has approved it; final Union Cabinet approval still required before launch.
programmes.quote: Rs 20,000 crore (~$2.4 bn) five-year CCUS scheme covering power, steel, cement, refining and chemicals

programmes.awarded_note: €200m pre-allocated to BASF/Air Liquide's Kairos@C at Antwerp; the remaining €1bn goes to a competitive round in 2028.
programmes.quote: €1.2 billion earmarked for CCS ... €200 million pre-allocated to BASF/Air Liquide's Kairos@C

known_gaps: Drawdown is published for only four of these programmes (US BIL, US DAC hubs, Norway Longship, Flanders). For the rest, awarded_to_date is null because no source states it — including the UK's £21.7bn, the largest commitment here. A null must not be rendered as zero.
This register covers GOVERNMENT programmes only. Private and corporate CCS investment is substantial and is tracked separately through the news corpus, where it is labelled by funder type.

Coverage follows the sources available, not a systematic global survey. A country absent from this register may still have public CCS funding — most of these entries come from the GCCSI 2024 report's country chapters, which are selective, plus programmes that surfaced in the news window.

Currency conversion to A$ uses the dashboard's fixed reference rates. For multi-decade programmes the real exchange-rate path will differ substantially; the A$ figures are for ordering countries against each other, not for budgeting.
Programmes marked scope 'ccs-eligible' fund more than CCS. Their headline value overstates CCS-specific money and they are shown separately from ccs-specific pots for that reason.
Japan's figure is derived (20% of a US$130bn bond, as the report says is expected), not stated. It is the only derived amount in this register and is flagged in its own note.
